## Verdict for DG0 round 19: FAIL I'm failing the gate on one Medium finding. The Landlock fix itself works, the history repair is sound, and all tests and the pre-freeze pass. I reviewed the frozen candidate `sha256:6720ad2c…922a` (commit `0a65201`). The candidate ID recomputes correctly, and the only commit after the freeze changes metadata. **New findings** | ID | Severity | Mandatory violation | Summary | |---|---|---|---| | F-DG0-154 | **Medium** | No | Threat-model residual 7 describes the wrong scope, so it is larger than disclosed.
• The process sandbox creates only an IPC namespace and binds the host `/proc` (`agent_sandbox.py:154-155`). So the `/proc/sys` settings a file tool can write are the host's single global kernel settings, shared by the host and every concurrent run. `threat-model.md:60` calls them "of its own run".
• It also says D-033 closed a cross-run path to another run's `/proc/sys`. That path doesn't exist separately, because every run already sees the same host `/proc`.
• It says `/proc/sys` is read-only for the agent's shell. My own shell's top `/proc` mount is read-write and shares the host's hostname (UTS) namespace, so the mount flags don't support that claim.
• I proposed a corrected text, a fresh user decision on D-030 option A, and a spike for a narrower control. | | F-DG0-155 | Low | No | D-035's tolerance of a missing `source_commit` (`rules.mjs:808-822`) also covers the gate's own round, not just superseded rounds. My repro: a non-existent gate `source_commit` passes current-mode validation with 0 errors, and only historical mode rejects it. The candidate content is still bound. | | F-DG0-156 | Low | No | Commit `5a49719` adds project allow rules for `git push`, `filter-branch`, `update-ref` and `branch` to `.claude/settings.json`. Every agent run loads project settings, so these commands skip the permission check for all agents. The sandbox still contains them (`.git` is read-only, no network). I'd accept this as an observation. | **Verifications of my earlier findings** - **F-DG0-152 (High): closed and verified.** The unit test ran fully, not skipped. Its control reproduced the original cross-run write and signal without Landlock; with Landlock both were refused, while the run's own areas and nested bubblewrap still worked. A live check on this run confirms `/proc/1/root` is refused. `landlock_exec.py` refuses to start `claude` if Landlock can't be applied. - **F-DG0-153: closed and verified.** Row 1 of the threat model is now correct. - **F-DG0-147: re-accepted as an observation.** It still fails safe for gate integrity. F-DG0-150/151 and `--unshare-ipc` still hold. - **F-DG0-149: stays OPEN (FAIL).** I can't accept it as an observation while residual 7 describes a per-run scope that doesn't exist (F-DG0-154). **D-034 history check: sound.** `checkWriteOnce` reports 0 errors. Both restored round-17 files are at blobs `862693f` and `276e32c`, first added in their original auto-commit. All 89 rewritten commits match the backup ref apart from those two files, and nothing under reviews, runs or candidates was ever deleted. **Other checks** - **Passed:** 93/93 tests, the pre-freeze in a fresh clone, the secrets scan (including the transcripts added since round 18) and the CI workflow check (unchanged since round 18). - **BLOCKED:** whether the shell layer actually refuses `/proc/sys` writes. Confirming that needs a real write, which the assignment forbids, so I didn't attempt one. **Requirements checked:** REQ-DLV-006, 007, 013, 016, 017, 022, 023, 026. I removed the disposable clone after the checks. Files are in `docs/delivery/`: - `reviews/DG0/round-19/code-security-reviewer.json` (schema-valid) - `reviews/DG0/round-19/code-security-reviewer.findings.json` - `reviews/DG0/round-19/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json` - `test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-19/`: six logs and the D-035 repro script
